ADDRESS.comment: Accepted `str` subclass keys can remain distinct mapping keys while canonicalizing to the same base-string key; key-only sorting would preserve emitted order when their values differ.
ADDRESS.why: The revised plan and behavior specification lock lexicographic sorting of each complete `(base_key, base_value)` pair. They require direct-hasher and `ResponseCacheKeyFactory(CanonicalFeatureHasher())` regressions with equal base keys, distinct values, and opposite emitted orders; this input remains valid and is neither rejected nor deduplicated.

ADDRESS.comment: `str(key)` / `str(value)` can invoke an accepted `str` subclass override of `__str__`, allowing identity drift or collisions.
ADDRESS.why: The locked contract keeps `str.__str__(key)` and `str.__str__(value)` after runtime validation and requires hostile-subclass regressions against a plain-`str` baseline.

ADDRESS.comment: An unpaired surrogate is a runtime `str`, but `ensure_ascii=False` followed by strict UTF-8 encoding raises `UnicodeEncodeError`.
ADDRESS.why: The locked error policy translates only that UTF-8 boundary error into `TypeError` chained from the original `UnicodeEncodeError`; direct-hasher and factory non-wrapping/no-key regressions are required.
